d: The Deputy Operations Manager supports the Operations Manager in planning, Executing, coordinating, and controlling inspection services operations and project delivery. This role helps ensure that inspection, testing, NDT, quality, and other assigned services are executed on schedule, within approved budgets, and in accordance with client requirements, applicable standards, contractual obligations, and company procedures.

The position coordinates jobs resources, site activities, equipment, reports, and client interfaces; monitors operational performance and commercial risks; and supports business growth. The Deputy Operations Manager acts on behalf of the Operations Manager when delegated.
Developing operational plans, priorities, budgets, forecasts, and resource plans for assigned jobs and services.
Coordinate the assigned jobs throughout the entire lifecycle, including mobilization, service delivery, report preparation and submission, invoicing support, and project close-out.
Review scopes of work, contractual requirements, client specifications, inspection and test plans, procedures, schedules, and deliverables; clarify gaps before execution.
Coordinate availability and deployment of competent personnel, inspectors, NDT technicians, engineers, equipment, tools, consumables, and approved subcontractors.
Monitor productivity, utilization, schedule performance, costs, overtime, subcontracting, and gross margin; identify variances and recommend corrective actions.
Ensure required personnel qualifications and authorizations, equipment calibration, method/procedure approvals before work proceeds.
Maintain effective communication with clients and resolve operational issues and escalate significant risks promptly.
Review the status and quality of technical reports, timesheets, service entries, client approvals, and supporting documents required for timely invoicing and collection follow-up.
Support recruitment, onboarding, competency development, performance monitoring, coaching, and succession planning for operational personnel, as assigned.
Identify opportunities to improve processes, service quality, resource utilization and operational efficiency; support proposals and new business opportunities with Sales.
Perform other duties assigned by the Operations Manager and deputize for the Operations Manager within delegated authority.
Bachelor’s degree in engineering or equivalent technical discipline.
Must hold relevant internationally recognized certifications, such as Certified Welding Inspector (CWI/CSWIP), BGAS, API 653, or API 510.

At least 8–10 years of relevant experience in industrial services, inspection, testing, NDT, QA/QC, or oil and gas projects, including demonstrated experience coordinating multiple projects or operational teams. Experience in a TIC company specially in Oman is preferred.
Good communication, reporting, leadership, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, procedures and quality records.
Travel Requirements: Frequent travel to project sites, fabrication facilities and vendor locations within the UAE as required.
Work Area: Industrial Plants, Energy & Environmental Technology
Company: TUV SUD Middle East Co. SPC

Tivoli Hotels & Resorts is a collection of luxury hotels and resorts set in idyllic beaches and cosmopolitan locations, from iconic destinations in Europe to the Middle East, and from Brazil to Asia. We are timeless, dedicated, and distinctive — evoking a time when hotel stays were grand experiences and travel meant life slowed down for a while.

Founded in 1933, Tivoli’s long-standing heritage is built on extraordinary service, authentic local experiences, and a genuine dedication to the art of hospitality. If you share a passion for making every guest feel they have arrived somewhere truly special, Tivoli is where your story belongs.

This role is critical in establishing and managing all government relations, regulatory compliance, and administrative processes for both Tivoli Bilaj Al Jazayer Bahrain Resort and Avani Bilaj Al Jazayer Bahrain Resort.

You will be responsible for ensuring the smooth and timely processing of government documentation, employee visas, work permits, residence permits, and other statutory requirements. Acting as the primary liaison between the resorts and government authorities in Bahrain, you will ensure full compliance with local laws and regulations while supporting the successful pre-opening and ongoing operations of both properties.
Manage and process employee work permits, residence visas, visa renewals, cancellations, and related immigration requirements in accordance with Bahrain regulations.
Lead the pre-opening setup of government relations processes, including company registrations, licensing, employee immigration documentation, and regulatory approvals for both properties.

Liaise with relevant government authorities, including the Labour Market Regulatory Authority (LMRA), Nationality, Passports and Residence Affairs (NPRA), Ministry of Labour, and other relevant regulatory bodies.
Coordinate with government departments to secure and renew all necessary hotel licenses, permits, and approvals to ensure uninterrupted operations.
Ensure full compliance with Bahrain labour laws, immigration regulations, and government policies.
Maintain accurate and confidential records of employee immigration documents, work permits, residence permits, and other government-related documentation.
Monitor the validity and expiration dates of visas, permits, licenses, and statutory documents, ensuring timely renewals.
Support the People & Culture department with new employee onboarding, immigration formalities, medical appointments, and other government-related requirements.
Establish and maintain effective professional relationships with government officials and regulatory authorities.
Stay updated on changes in government regulations, labour laws, immigration policies, and compliance requirements, advising management of their implications.
Coordinate government inspections and audits, ensuring all required documentation is available and compliant.
Manage government-related administrative expenses, application fees, and documentation costs while maintaining accurate financial records.
Provide regular reports to management on visa status, work permit applications, government transactions, compliance matters, and pending approvals.
Collaborate closely with People & Culture, Finance, Security, and Operations teams to ensure efficient coordination of all government-related activities.

Support the Hotel General Manager and People & Culture leadership with guidance on government regulations, regulatory compliance, and administrative requirements during pre-opening and post-launch operations.

This role is ideal for a proactive and detail-oriented Government Relations professional with strong knowledge of Bahrain's government procedures, excellent relationships with local authorities, and the ability to manage regulatory requirements for two international hospitality brands within a dynamic resort environment.
q: Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Human Resources, Public Administration, or a related field.
Minimum 2–3 years of experience in a Government Relations Officer (GRO/PRO) role, preferably within the hospitality industry in Bahrain.
Strong working knowledge of Bahrain labour laws, immigration regulations, and government administrative procedures.
Proven experience dealing with LMRA, NPRA, Ministry of Labour, and other relevant government authorities.
Experience managing work permits, residence visas, company licenses, and regulatory approvals.
Previous hotel pre-opening experience would be an advantage.
Fluency in Arabic and English, both written and spoken, is essential.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and relevant Bahrain government online portals.
Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and handle confidential information with discretion.
Valid Bahrain driving license would be an advantage.
Reporting into the Hotel General Manager, with close functional coordination with the People & Culture Department.
